item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 151135
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sat Aug 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located a couple hundred miles east-southeast of Hilo,
Hawaii.

The National Hurricane Center is also issuing advisories on
Tropical Depression Hernan, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form several hundred miles south of
the coast of southern Mexico near the middle portion of next week.
Some gradual development of this system is possible, while the
system moves westward or west-northwestward well south of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

Western Portion of the East Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well to the west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula by the middle of next
week. Gradual development of this system is possible thereafter
while it moves generally westward across the western portion of the
east Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Berg

item.title: Tropical Depression Hernan Public Advisory Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Aug 15 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 151431
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Hernan Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP082026
500 AM HST Sat Aug 15 2026
 
...HERNAN EXPECTED TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.1N 134.9W
ABOUT 1690 MI...2720 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Hernan
was located near latitude 16.1 North, longitude 134.9 West. The
depression is moving toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h) and this
general motion is expected to continue through the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Slow weakening is forecast during the few days, and Hernan is 
forecast to degenerate to a remnant low pressure area later today.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Berg

item.title: Tropical Depression Hernan Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Fri Aug 14 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 150837
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Depression Hernan Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP082026
1100 PM HST Fri Aug 14 2026

Hernan is currently a swirl of low- to mid-level clouds with no 
active convection. A recent ASCAT overpass showed winds of 25-27 kt 
in the northwestern quadrant, and based on this and the possibility 
of undersampling the initial intensity is held at a possibly 
generous 30 kt. Unless convection makes a significant re-appearance, 
the cyclone is expected to degenerate to a remnant low within the 
next 12 h. The new forecast calls for the remnant low to decay to a 
trough by 72 h in agreement with the global models.

The initial motion is 275/11 kt. A low- to mid-level ridge to the 
north should steer Hernan and its remnants westward for the next 
few days. The new forecast track is similar to, but a little faster 
than, the previous track.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
